title: HE WANTED A GRAND MIRACLE.
paragraphs: HE WANTED A GRAND MIRACLE.

Trumpets.
Thunder.
A prophet waving his hand dramatically over diseased skin.
Instead?
God gave him muddy water.
And Naaman almost missed his miracle because it looked… ordinary.
Stay with me.
THE MAN WHO HAD EVERYTHING—EXCEPT CLEAN SKIN
(2 Kings 5)
Naaman was not a weak man. He was a war hero. Commander of the army of Aram. Decorated. Respected. Feared.

But under the armor…
Leprosy.

White patches spreading across strong brown skin.
Power on the outside.
Decay underneath.
Sound familiar?
Some scholars interpret his condition as a severe skin disease rather than modern Hansen’s disease. But Scripture is clear: it made him unclean. Untouchable. Slowly dying.
And pride doesn’t like to admit that.
HE EXPECTED FIRE FROM HEAVEN
He travels with silver, gold, designer garments—because powerful men think blessings can be purchased.
He stands at the door of Elisha’s house expecting drama.
Instead, the prophet doesn’t even come out.
Just a message:
“Go and wash in the Jordan seven times.” (2 Kings 5:10)
That’s it.

No prayer meeting.
No oil anointing.
No spotlight.
Just… water.
And not even clean water. The Jordan was murky. Brown. Common.
Naaman explodes.
“Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?” (2 Kings 5:12)
Translation?
“I didn’t come all this way for something this simple.”
Let me talk to somebody.

You wanted a grand miracle.
God gave you daily obedience.

You wanted a prophetic word.
God gave you forgiveness and told you to repent.

You wanted instant healing.
God gave you a process.
And pride says, “This can’t be it.”
THE TURN — MUDDY WATER BECAME HOLY
Here’s the open loop closing.
Naaman’s servants speak truth:
“If the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it?” (2 Kings 5:13)
In other words—

You’d climb mountains.
You’d bleed for it.
You’d fast for 40 days.
But you won’t bend.
So Naaman goes down.
Catch that.
He goes down into the Jordan.
Seven times.
Not six. Not “symbolic.” Seven.
And when he comes up the seventh time—
His skin is restored like that of a young boy. (2 Kings 5:14)
Fresh. Soft. Clean.
The miracle was always waiting on humility.
THIS ISN’T ABOUT WATER.
It’s about pride.
It’s about the scandal of simple obedience.
Naaman wanted spectacle.
God wanted surrender.
And this is where it points to Jesus.
Because the Gospel is offensively simple.

Repent.
Believe.
Receive grace.

No ladder to climb.
No performance to polish.
Just a cross.
And pride hates that.

We want to earn it.
We want to deserve it.
We want a grand miracle.

But salvation came through something that looked weak—
A crucified Savior.
Scripture says, “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.” (James 4:6)
Naaman dipped in muddy water.
We bow at a bloody cross.

And in both cases—
Grace meets humility.
TO THE ONE FRUSTRATED WITH “SIMPLE OBEDIENCE”
You keep waiting for fireworks.
But maybe your miracle is hidden in:

• Confessing that sin
• Forgiving that person
• Showing up consistently
• Praying when you feel nothing
• Serving when no one claps
Don’t despise the Jordan.
Your pride is louder than the water.
But grace is deeper.
THE INVITATION
Maybe your leprosy isn’t on your skin.

Maybe it’s secret sin.
Addiction.
Bitterness.
Religious pride.
You don’t need a grand display.
You need to go down.

Repent.
Trust Christ.
Obey what He already said.

Jesus doesn’t ask you to perform.
He asks you to surrender.
And when you do—

What shame tried to rot,
Grace will restore.
